lines.text: HOA homes sell for about 4% more. Worth it?
lines.say: HOA homes sell for about four percent more. Worth it?

lines.text: A 2019 study put it at about $13,500 over similar non-HOA homes.
lines.say: A twenty nineteen study put it at about thirteen thousand five hundred dollars over similar non-HOA homes.

lines.text: HOA residents grew from about 2 million in 1970 to about 74 million in 2020.
lines.say: HOA residents grew from about two million in nineteen seventy to about seventy-four million in twenty twenty.

lines.text: In 2024, 1 in 4 owners paid a condo or HOA fee, median $135 a month.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-four, one in four owners paid a condo or HOA fee, median one hundred thirty-five dollars a month.

lines.text: Pros: perks, common areas, curb appeal. Cons: rising fees, rules, fines, surprise bills.
lines.say: Pros: perks, common areas, curb appeal. Cons: rising fees, rules, fines, surprise bills.

lines.text: Our math: $300 a month for 10 years is $36,000.
lines.say: Our math: three hundred dollars a month for ten years is thirty-six thousand dollars.

lines.text: Lenders count those dues in your debt-to-income ratio, so they can shrink what you can borrow.
lines.say: Lenders count those dues in your debt-to-income ratio, so they can shrink what you can borrow.

lines.text: The surprise: in most states, an HOA can foreclose over unpaid dues, though rules vary.
lines.say: The surprise: in most states, an HOA can foreclose over unpaid dues, though rules vary.

lines.text: Buyers often check fee history, rules, reserves and past assessments.

post.title: HOA homes sell for about 4% more. Is the fee worth it?
post.ig:
HOA homes sell for about 4% more. Is it worth the fee?
A 2019 study found HOA homes priced at least 4% (about $13,500) above similar homes outside one.
In 2024, about 1 in 4 US owners paid a condo or HOA fee; the median was $135 a month.
Our math: $300 a month for 10 years is $36,000, and lenders count dues in your debt-to-income ratio.
In most states an HOA can foreclose over unpaid dues. Rules vary by state.
Sources: Journal of Urban Economics (2019), US Census Bureau ACS 2024, Foundation for Community Association Research.
News and education, not financial advice.
